correctness.rationale: For \(|f|\le1\), the Poisson boundary trace has \(\sum_{n\ne0}|c_n|^2\le1-a^2\). A two-sign Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives \(B_f(r)\le a+\sqrt{2(1-a^2)}r/\sqrt{1-r^2}\), hence \(R_H(a)\ge\sqrt{(1-a)/(3+a)}\). The unimodular smooth witness \(e^{i\varepsilon\cos t}\) has center magnitude \(1-\varepsilon^2/4+O(\varepsilon^4)\) and total first Fourier modulus \(\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^3)\), giving the matching upper bound \((1/2+o(1))\sqrt{1-a}\). The map \(\varepsilon\mapsto a\) is invertible close to zero, covering every sufficiently near-one center. The terminal case follows from the harmonic maximum principle. Strict dominance over the source formula is an exact inequality for all \(a<1\).

value.rationale: The source announces a best-possible fixed-center Bohr radius whose dependence on the center is linear. The accepted theorem supplies a strict global improvement and a sharp square-root degeneration with exact coefficient one-half. The simultaneous energy bound and a matching unimodular Poisson perturbation explain why degreewise sharpness cannot justify a global sharp radius. This resolves the leading asymptotic of a natural, explicitly motivated invariant and reveals the endpoint jump, rather than changing a cosmetic normalization.
